title: The Buckwheat (The Warning of the Willow)

full_text:
Beside the peaceful field of wheat and rye stood the haughty buckwheat, raising its white blossoms with defiant pride, boasting that it surpassed all neighboring crops in beauty and wealth.

When the black clouds of the thunderstorm rolled over the plains, the ancient willow tree called out: "Bow your head, little flower! The spirit of the storm flies on wings of fire!"

The golden wheat and slender oats bowed in quiet reverence, yielding to the tempest; but the proud buckwheat stood stiff and upright, sneering at their humility.

A blinding flash of lightning split the heavens, and the deafening thunder shook the plain. When the sun broke through the clouds, the wheat and oats lifted their heads, refreshed and sparkling with raindrops; but the haughty buckwheat lay charred, shriveled, and dead—destroyed by its own stubborn pride.
moral: He who refuses to bow before the majestic laws of nature is broken by the storm.
